proposal.hypothesis: A rectangular footprint imposes unsupported corner wedges on observed convex buildings with oblique or clipped corners. A convex hull of the same robustly bounded observed XY support can reduce this geometric over-completion while preserving the convex clipping pipeline.
changed_behavior: Keep the existing minimum-rectangle orientation and projected quantile bounds.
When retained XY support has at least three distinct non-collinear points, replace the rectangle footprint with its counterclockwise convex hull.
Retain the rectangle fallback for insufficient support and record the selected footprint rule in model metrics.
proposal.expected_benefit: Avoid imposing orthogonal rectangular corners where the input supports a different convex boundary; roof clipping, walls and base all use the same selected footprint.
risks: Concave footprints and courtyards remain unsupported; K01 is addressed only for observed convex boundary shape.
Incomplete boundary observations may shrink the hull below the true building footprint.
Spurious points inside the existing quantile bounds can still expand the hull.
Additional boundary vertices can increase mesh complexity.

proposal.hypothesis: The fixed 60-return support floor and strict exclusion of height-quantile ties can starve otherwise planar roof candidates in sparse or flat scans. A single input-only recovery attempt, gated on complete baseline plane failure, may recover supported meshes while preserving successful baseline reconstructions.
changed_behavior: Only after baseline plane extraction returns zero planes, retry the existing normal and curvature filter with inclusive numerical ties at the input z 25th percentile.

Use a retry support floor max(12, min(60, ceil(0.15 * retry_candidate_count))), while retaining the original 7.5-percent floor, slope and residual limits, 550 hypotheses, eight-stage limit, and deterministic seed 739.
Record whether recovery was used and its support floor. Preserve inferred base/wall labels, existing metrics, dependencies, and module.run interface.
proposal.expected_benefit: Potentially reduce complete No roof plane supported failures for sparse or tied-height roofs. No expected change for inputs whose baseline extracts at least one plane.
risks: Feedback provides the failure category, not proof of candidate starvation; other causes may remain.
Lower support can admit accidental planes and smaller structures into convex global-envelope selection.
Including cutoff ties can admit low horizontal surfaces; no terrain claim follows.
This does not address the localized real-data footprint and multi-height mismatches or prove improved geometric accuracy.
